title: Scout & Signal Playbook for Emerging Model Features and Threats
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create an operational playbook and automated signal pipeline to proactively scout new model releases, emergent model features, and competitive threats. The playbook defines signal sources, a scoring rubric for feature priority, alert thresholds, triage workflow, and templated follow-up asks for engineering, research, and GTM. Output: a repeatable workflow that reduces blindspots and shortens time-to-response for features that affect Redwood's product positioning (e.g., tool-calling, structured output guarantees, KV cache compatibility, quantization-friendly variants, and latency/throughput improvements).
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests at least 6 signal sources (Hugging Face model releases, arXiv/filter, Twitter/X model announcements, partner briefings, internal eval telemetry, customer tickets)
Automated scoring rubric assigns top-20 signals weekly; 3 signal triage cards auto-created in Linear when threshold crossed
Triage template includes: impact assessment, required eng effort estimate, suggested mitigation/advantage play, and recommended owners
Dashboard tile in Console shows emerging-feature velocity and top risk models
First run completes and creates actionable follow-ups for two prioritized signals

decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose hybrid scoring (heuristic + telemetry) vs pure manual; trade-off: faster automation but needs guardrails
2026-03-12: Prioritized inclusion of customer tickets and internal eval telemetry as high-fidelity signals despite lower volume
2026-03-13: Decided to surface only P1/P2 model signals to GTM to avoid noise; keep lower priority signals for research digest
tradeoffs: Automated ingestion increases coverage but introduces noisy signals — mitigated by combined heuristic+telemetry scoring and manual triage
Catch-all alerts may create workstream churn; solution: threshold tuning and weekly digest for P3 signals
Scoring complexity vs transparency — chose simpler 5-factor rubric initially with plan to evolve to ML-ranking later
scoring_rubric: Compatibility Cost (0-10): infra changes required for Redwood runtime
Regression Risk (0-10): likelihood of killing existing behaviours
Economic Impact (0-10): per-token or infra cost delta
Security/Compliance Risk (0-10): data handling or export concerns
alert_thresholds: High alert: score >=36 -> auto-create Linear triage (P1) and notify Product, Eng on Slack #model-signals
Medium alert: score 25-35 -> include in Friday digest and tag Research
Low alert: score <25 -> bagged in monthly scout report
signal_sources: Model devs' Twitter/X announcements and blog posts
Internal eval harness telemetry (regressions, latency wins)
Open-source quantization releases and kernels (QAT/INT8 variants)
